extracted.intended_audience: BBC News readers and journalists interested in media verification
extracted.subtask_short: verifying images and videos for authenticity
extracted.subtask_description: Marking third-party images and videos as 'verified' by embedding provenance metadata, cryptographically binding it, applying investigative checks (weather, landmarks, shadows, timestamps), and presenting an explanatory 'How we verified this' trail to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded metadata and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: A verified video or image has its metadata including the author, the date it was taken, location, camera details and any subsequent edits or changes embedded into the content, allowing readers and viewers to check its authenticity and chain of provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed comprehensive metadata fields (author, date, location, camera details, edit history) directly into the file so consumers can inspect origin and modification history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptographic binding of metadata to content
rubrics_metrics.description: As well as cryptographically binding the metadata to the content, BBC staff use standard investigatory techniques to check its authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cryptographic methods so metadata is tamper-evident and cannot be altered without detection; pair technical guarantees with human checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the C2PA Content Credentials standard
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC News has adopted the Content Credentials standard from the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) to authenticate videos and photos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt interoperable, industry-backed standards (C2PA) for embedding provenance and credentials; note that major tech companies and tools (Adobe, Microsoft, Google, OpenAI/Dall‑E 3) support the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit trail and controlled metadata editing
rubrics_metrics.description: C2PA defines a secure way for metadata and an audit trail to be embedded into digital content. The author decides what metadata to include initially, and can edit the data too, but no other parties can change it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an auditable edit-history attached to content; ensure only authorized parties (original author) can modify the declared metadata while preserving immutability for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigatory check — weather consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Checking if the weather in a photo or video matches the conditions on the day it was purportedly taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare visible weather cues (cloud cover, lighting, precipitation) against meteorological records or contemporaneous imagery to spot inconsistencies that suggest manipulation or misdating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigatory check — landmark and physical-feature matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing if physical features match real items at the location (for example, matching gravestones, a large tree and other landmarks to existing images found on Google Maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geolocation tools and publicly available imagery (Google Maps, street view, archival photos) to confirm that features in content correspond to the stated location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigatory check — shadow direction and time-of-day consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the direction of shadows observed to determine the likely time of day the footage was filmed (e.g., shadows indicating morning filming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze shadow length and direction relative to known sun positions for the claimed date/location to validate timestamp claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to audiences — 'How we verified this' explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verified content on the BBC News site is accompanied by a button reading 'How we verified this' that explains the verification steps taken and provenance details (e.g., first upload time, matched landmarks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, human-readable provenance statement alongside verified content so readers can see what checks were performed and why the content is considered authentic, increasing trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing source uploads and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenting and checking platform provenance (for example: 'The video from the cemetery was first uploaded to TikTok on Saturday 2 March at 1750G (1250 local)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and verify original upload times, platform sources, and any available metadata to build a timeline of the content's origin and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority verification for conflict-area footage and manipulated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Footage from areas of conflict is notoriously prone to manipulation for propaganda purposes, with video repurposed from previous conflicts, edited convincingly or created from scratch. The aim of verification is to counter AI-generated and altered content presented as reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply heightened scrutiny to content from high-risk contexts (conflict zones, viral social-media posts) using both technical provenance and targeted human-led checks to guard against deepfakes, repurposing, and propaganda.
